item.title: #!/bin/bash or #!/usr/bin/env sh
item.description:
A shebang names the interpreter; the forms differ in where they look.

#!/bin/bash runs the binary at that exact path: Bash features work — arrays, [[ ]], brace expansion, source — but it breaks where Bash is absent or elsewhere: minimal containers, some BSDs.

#!/usr/bin/env sh asks env to find sh on the user’s PATH, so it runs under whatever sh is — dash on Ubuntu, bash in POSIX mode, else something else. Portable, POSIX features only. Same for #!/usr/bin/env bash: it finds a Bash, not a specific one.
